function: hyperDISTA, an unfolded ISTA detector with a hypernetwork, recovers QPSK/16QAM symbols in massive MIMO across channel scenarios, with semi-supervised retraining for unseen ones (pp. 1, 5-6).
system: Massive MIMO detection with 16 transmit and 64 receive antennas (also 64x64), QPSK and 16QAM; no RIS; frequency band not stated (pp. 7, 10).
method: Deep-unfolded ISTA network (18 layers, convolutional sparse transform) with gated hypernetwork setting step size and threshold; supervised multi-scenario training, semi-supervised pseudo-label retraining with MMSE labels (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: Custom simulator: i.i.d. Rician-type channels (Gaussian entries, means 0-1) and Kronecker-correlated channels (coefficient 0-0.9), Rayleigh at mean 0 (pp. 7, 10-11).
test_conditions: Seen: trained on three scenarios, tested on each. Unseen: tested on other Gaussian means or correlation coefficients after retraining with 2,560 unlabelled samples (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned: EP algorithm, MMSE; learned: DISTA trained per scenario, MMNet, HyperEPNet; hyperDISTA without retraining (pp. 8-11).
metrics: Symbol error rate versus SNR, channel mean or correlation coefficient (pp. 8-12).
complexity: Per-iteration complexity orders for hyperDISTA, DISTA, MMSE, AMP, EP (p. 7); 157,482 trainable parameters versus 182,277 for HyperEPNet (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 7: "The experiment considers two types of channels: i.i.d. Rician" fading and correlated channels, with "scenario is generated according to the Kronecker model [34]". Custom simulator with textbook models: no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "under the channel scenarios that are different from the training" ones, for the retrained hyperDISTA using "the number of unlabeled data collected in the new channel scenario is 2, 560"; p. 11: "hyperDISTA trained on i.i.d. Rician channel generalizes well to the i.i.d. Rayleigh channel".
q3_support: p. 9: "compare the performance of hyperDISTA with DISTA, MMNet, hyperEPNet and the EP algorithm" in SER (Figs. 6-9); p. 11: Fig. 10 compares also with MMSE. DISTA, MMNet and HyperEPNet are earlier learned detectors; EP and MMSE are non-learned.
q4_support: p. 7: "we provide the computational complexity analysis of the hyperDISTA network" (order per iteration, compared with MMSE, AMP, EP); p. 8: "the total number of trainable parameters in hyperDISTA is 157482".
q5_support: p. 7: "The code is implemented in Pytorch, and the computing" platform is a CPU with a GPU; no code or data link, data generated by the authors' own simulator.
notes: Included as area 1 (deep-unfolded detector with trained parameters). q2 rests on Figs. 10-13: testing on Gaussian means or correlation coefficients absent from training, after pseudo-label retraining on 2,560 unlabelled samples, and Fig. 10 also tests hyperDISTA without retraining on unseen means. q3 learned baselines: DISTA ([24], same authors), MMNet [22], HyperEPNet [31]; non-learned: EP, MMSE.
